key_insight: For pulmonary embolism risk stratification, medical records and cardiac biomarkers outperformed vascular features, and even graph neural networks on vascular trees did not add predictive value.
clinical_relevance: This suggests that routine risk assessment may rely more on readily available tabular clinical data than on increasingly complex vascular graph modeling from CTPA.
method: Benchmark tabular models using medical records plus cardiac biomarkers
Add vascular biomarkers extracted from CTPA to assess incremental value
Test graph neural networks on the vascular tree’s intrinsic graph representation
evidence_signal: The study used a private fully annotated cohort of 353 patients with complete data and found no improvement from vascular biomarkers or vascular-graph GNNs over strong tabular baselines.
watch_item: Results come from a single private dataset, so the apparent lack of vascular-graph signal may not generalize to other centers, scanners, or patient populations.
paper_title: Pulmonary Embolism Risk Stratification from CTPA and Medical Records: Vascular Graphs Are Not All You Need
